at padle.explanation: "At padle" means "to paddle", to move a small boat by pushing the water with a paddle. When you paddle, you face forward. At ro (to row) is different: with oars you sit with your back to where you are going.

sentence.da: Vi kan **padle** hen over søen i en kano.
sentence.en: We can paddle across the lake in a canoe.

at pakke.explanation: "At pakke" means "to pack", for example a suitcase or a bag: Jeg pakker min kuffert (I pack my suitcase). It also means "to wrap": pakke en gave ind (to wrap a present). En pakke (a parcel) looks the same.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **pakke** min kuffert i dag.
sentence.en: I want to pack my suitcase today.

at pakke ud.explanation: "At pakke ud" means "to unpack", and also "to unwrap": Jeg pakker tasken ud (I unpack the bag). Børnene pakker gaver ud (The children unwrap presents).

sentence.da: Vi kan **pakke ud**, når vi kommer til hotellet.
sentence.en: We can unpack when we get to the hotel.

at parkere.explanation: "At parkere" means "to park", a car or a bike: Kan jeg parkere her? (Can I park here?) A common sign is Parkering forbudt (No parking).

sentence.da: Vi kan **parkere** bilen bag huset.
sentence.en: We can park the car behind the house.

at passe.explanation: "At passe" means "to fit" or "to suit": Jakken passer dig (The jacket fits you). It also means to look after: Jeg passer min lillebror (I am looking after my little brother).

sentence.da: Bukserne er for store og vil ikke **passe** mig.
sentence.en: The pants are too big and will not fit me.

at passe børn.explanation: "At passe børn" means "to babysit", and also "to look after children" in general: Jeg passer naboens børn om aftenen (I babysit the neighbor's kids in the evening). Animals work too: at passe en hund (to look after a dog).

related.en: to be careful, to look out

sentence.da: Jeg kan **passe børn**, når I går i biografen.
sentence.en: I can babysit when you go to the movies.

at passe ind.explanation: "At passe ind" means "to fit in", with a group or a place: Han passer godt ind på holdet (He fits in well on the team). It also works for things: Sofaen passer ind i stuen (The sofa fits into the living room).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **passe ind** på min nye skole.
sentence.en: I would like to fit in at my new school.

at passe på.explanation: "At passe på" means "to watch out", and also "to take care of": Pas på! (Watch out!). Pas på dig selv (Take care of yourself). Jeg passer på dine nøgler (I am looking after your keys).

forms.en: I have taken care / watched out

sentence.da: Du skal **passe på**, når du krydser vejen.
sentence.en: You have to watch out when you cross the road.

at passe til.explanation: "At passe til" means "to go with" or "to suit": Skjorten passer til bukserne (The shirt goes with the pants). It also works for people: Jobbet passer til dig (The job suits you).

sentence.da: Den røde jakke vil **passe til** dine sko.
sentence.en: The red jacket will go with your shoes.

at passere.explanation: "At passere" means "to pass", going by a place: Vi passerer broen (We pass the bridge). To pass a test, use at bestå (to pass): Jeg bestod prøven (I passed the test).

sentence.da: Vi skal **passere** en lille by på vejen.
sentence.en: We have to pass a small town on the way.

at pege.explanation: "At pege" means "to point", and you point at something with på: Han pegede på mig (He pointed at me).

sentence.da: Du kan **pege** på det, du vil have.
sentence.en: You can point at what you want.

at pege på.explanation: "At pege på" means "to point to" or "to point at": Hun peger på bogen (She points at the book).

sentence.da: Du skal **pege på** det rigtige billede.
sentence.en: You have to point to the right picture.

at pendle.explanation: "At pendle" means "to commute", to go back and forth between home and work or school, often a long way: Jeg pendler fra Køge til København (I commute from Køge to Copenhagen). A person who does this is en pendler (a commuter).

sentence.da: Hun vil ikke **pendle** to timer hver dag til arbejde.
sentence.en: She does not want to commute two hours every day to work.

at piske.explanation: "At piske" means "to whisk" and "to whip", mixing air into eggs or cream with fast strokes: Vi pisker fløde (We whip cream).

sentence.da: Han skal **piske** æggene og sukkeret.
sentence.en: He has to whisk the eggs and the sugar.

at pjække.explanation: "At pjække" means "to skip school", to stay away from lessons without a good reason. Danes also use it for work or training: Jeg pjækker fra træning (I am skipping practice).

forms.en: I have skipped school / played hooky

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **pjække**, men han har en prøve i dag.
sentence.en: He would like to skip school, but he has a test today.

at placere.explanation: "At placere" means "to place" or "to put" in a particular spot: Jeg placerer stolen ved vinduet (I place the chair by the window). It also means to give someone a seat: Jeg placerer dig her (I will seat you here).

sentence.da: Du kan **placere** tasken ved døren.
sentence.en: You can put the bag by the door.

at plage.explanation: "At plage" means "to pester" or "to torment", to keep after someone again and again. It works for people and for things like pain, worry or noise: Smerterne plager ham (The pain torments him). Børn kan plage deres forældre om slik (Children can pester their parents for candy).

sentence.da: Støjen fra vejen begynder at **plage** os om natten.
sentence.en: The noise from the road is starting to torment us at night.

at planlægge.explanation: "At planlægge" means "to plan", deciding ahead what will happen and when, for trips, parties or work: Vi planlægger en rejse til Italien (We are planning a trip to Italy).

sentence.da: Vi skal **planlægge** festen, før gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: We have to plan the party before the guests come.

at plante.explanation: "At plante" means "to plant", to put a tree, flower or seed in the ground: Jeg planter tulipaner i bedet (I plant tulips in the flower bed). What you plant is en plante (a plant).

sentence.da: Vi vil **plante** et æbletræ i haven.
sentence.en: We want to plant an apple tree in the garden.

at pleje.explanation: "At pleje" means "to usually (do)" and "to care for". The habit meaning is followed by at (to): Jeg plejer at gå tidligt i seng (I usually go to bed early). The care meaning is for sick people: Hun plejer sin syge far (She cares for her sick father).

forms.en: I usually do / I care for
I used to / I cared for

sentence.da: Sygeplejersken skal **pleje** patienterne hver dag.
sentence.en: The nurse has to care for the patients every day.

at plukke.explanation: "At plukke" means "to pick", to take fruit or flowers by hand from where they grow. It also means to pluck the feathers off a bird: at plukke en kylling (to pluck a chicken).

sentence.da: Vi kan **plukke** jordbær i haven, når de er røde.
sentence.en: We can pick strawberries in the garden when they are red.

at plyndre.explanation: "At plyndre" means "to plunder", to take everything valuable from a place, often by force during war or riots. It is also used playfully for raiding a place: Børnene plyndrer køleskabet (The kids raid the fridge).

sentence.da: Tyvene vil **plyndre** butikken og tage alt af værdi.
sentence.en: The thieves want to loot the store and take everything of value.

at poste.explanation: "At poste" means "to post" something online, like a photo or a message: Hun poster billeder hver dag (She posts photos every day). It can also mean to mail a letter: Jeg poster brevet i dag (I am mailing the letter today).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **poste** et billede fra turen.
sentence.en: I want to post a picture from the trip.

at praktisere.explanation: "At praktisere" means "to practice", to carry out a profession, a belief or an idea in real life: Hun praktiserer buddhisme (She practices Buddhism). It is not for repeating something to get better. For that, use at øve (to practice).

sentence.da: Man skal have en uddannelse for at **praktisere** som læge.
sentence.en: You need an education to practice as a doctor.

at presse.explanation: "At presse" means "to press", "to squeeze" and "to pressure": Jeg presser appelsiner (I squeeze oranges). Chefen presser os (The boss is pressuring us).

sentence.da: Hun vil **presse** citronen over fisken.
sentence.en: She wants to squeeze the lemon over the fish.

at printe.explanation: "At printe" means "to print" from a computer. For books and newspapers, Danes say at trykke (to print with a press).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **printe** billetten før turen.
sentence.en: I want to print the ticket before the trip.

at prioritere.explanation: "At prioritere" means "to prioritize", to decide what matters most and do that first when you cannot do everything: Jeg prioriterer min familie (I put my family first). It also fits money and time: at prioritere sin tid (to prioritize your time).

sentence.da: Man må **prioritere**, når der er for mange opgaver.
sentence.en: You have to prioritize when there are too many tasks.

at producere.explanation: "At producere" means "to produce", to make things in large amounts, usually to sell them. It also fits films and music: Hun producerer film (She produces films).

sentence.da: Fabrikken kan **producere** tusind biler om året.
sentence.en: The factory can produce a thousand cars a year.

at programmere.explanation: "At programmere" means "to program", to write instructions that a computer follows: Hun programmerer apps (She programs apps). It also means to set a machine to work by itself: at programmere en vaskemaskine (to program a washing machine).

sentence.da: Jeg vil lære at **programmere**, så jeg kan lave et spil.
sentence.en: I want to learn to program so I can make a game.

at protestere.explanation: "At protestere" means "to protest", to say or show that you do not accept something. What you protest against comes after mod (against): Folk protesterer mod den nye lov (People protest against the new law).

sentence.da: Mange mennesker vil **protestere** mod de høje priser.
sentence.en: Many people will protest against the high prices.

at præsentere.explanation: "At præsentere" means "to present" or "to introduce": Jeg vil gerne præsentere min ven (I would like to introduce my friend). Hun præsenterede planen (She presented the plan).

sentence.da: Må jeg **præsentere** min kone for dig?
sentence.en: May I introduce my wife to you?

at prøve.explanation: "At prøve" means "to try": Prøv at sige det igen (Try to say it again). It also means "to try on", for example prøve en kjole (to try on a dress). En prøve means "a test" or "a sample".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **prøve** at tale dansk.
sentence.en: I want to try to speak Danish.

at prøve på.explanation: "At prøve på" means "to try to", and an action follows with at: Jeg prøver på at sove (I am trying to sleep). Dropping på gives the same meaning: Jeg prøver at sove.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **prøve på** at lære flere danske ord.
sentence.en: I will try to learn more Danish words.

at prøve tøj.explanation: "At prøve tøj" means "to try on clothes", for example in a store. To ask about one item, you can say Må jeg prøve den? (May I try it on?).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **prøve tøj** i butikken.
sentence.en: I would like to try on clothes in the store.

at pudse.explanation: "At pudse" means "to polish" or "to clean until shiny", usually with a cloth. It is also the usual word for windows: Jeg pudser vinduer (I clean windows).

sentence.da: Han vil **pudse** skoene, fordi de er matte.
sentence.en: He wants to polish the shoes because they are dull.

at puste.explanation: "At puste" means "to blow" with your mouth: Hun puster på sin kaffe (She blows on her coffee). Puste ud (breathe out) also means "to take a break": Jeg puster ud efter løbeturen (I am catching my breath after the run).

sentence.da: Han skal **puste** på suppen, fordi den er varm.
sentence.en: He has to blow on the soup because it is hot.

at putte.explanation: "At putte" means "to put" something into a place, in a casual way and without much care: Jeg putter bogen i tasken (I put the book in the bag).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **putte** nøglerne i min lomme.
sentence.en: I want to put the keys in my pocket.

at pynte.explanation: "At pynte" means "to decorate": Vi pynter juletræet (We decorate the Christmas tree). With sig it means "to dress up": Hun pyntede sig til festen (She dressed up for the party).

sentence.da: Vi vil **pynte** stuen til festen i morgen.
sentence.en: We want to decorate the living room for the party tomorrow.

at påberåbe sig.explanation: "At påberåbe sig" means "to invoke", to point to a right, a rule or an excuse as your reason: påberåbe sig sin ret (to invoke your right). Sig changes with the person: jeg påberåber mig, du påberåber dig.

sentence.da: Hun kan **påberåbe sig** loven, når chefen ikke overholder aftalen.
sentence.en: She can invoke the law when the boss does not keep the agreement.

at pådrage sig.explanation: "At pådrage sig" means "to catch" an illness or "to pick up" an injury. It is also used for costs and trouble you bring on yourself: pådrage sig gæld (to run up debt). Sig changes with the person: jeg pådrager mig.

sentence.da: Hun kan **pådrage sig** en skade, når hun løber på is.
sentence.en: She can pick up an injury when she runs on ice.

at påføre.explanation: "At påføre" means "to inflict", to cause pain, damage or loss to someone. It also means "to apply" a layer onto a surface: påføre solcreme (to apply sunscreen). For catching something yourself, use at pådrage sig (to catch).

sentence.da: Stormen kan **påføre** byen store skader.
sentence.en: The storm can inflict great damage on the town.

at pålægge.explanation: "At pålægge" means "to impose", to make someone pay or do something by official decision: pålægge en afgift (to impose a tax). The same word gives pålæg (sandwich toppings), things you lay on top of the bread.

sentence.da: Staten vil **pålægge** bilerne en ny afgift.
sentence.en: The state wants to impose a new tax on cars.

at påpege.explanation: "At påpege" means "to point out", to say clearly that something is wrong or should be noticed: påpege en fejl (to point out a mistake). It is about speaking up, not about pointing with a finger. For that, use at pege (to point).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **påpege** fejlene i opgaven, og vi retter dem.
sentence.en: The teacher will point out the mistakes in the assignment, and we fix them.

at påstå.explanation: "At påstå" means "to claim", to say that something is true, often without showing proof: Han påstår, at han ikke vidste det (He claims that he did not know). It often sounds doubtful, as if the speaker does not quite believe it.

sentence.da: Hvordan kan du **påstå**, at du aldrig har set den?
sentence.en: How can you claim that you have never seen it?

at påtage sig.explanation: "At påtage sig" means "to take on", to agree to do a job or carry a duty. It often fits a heavy or official duty: påtage sig ansvaret (to take on the responsibility). Sig changes with the person: jeg påtager mig, du påtager dig.

sentence.da: Hun vil **påtage sig** opgaven, fordi ingen andre har tid.
sentence.en: She will take on the task because nobody else has time.

at påvirke.explanation: "At påvirke" means "to influence", to have an effect on how a person or thing feels, acts or turns out. It also describes what a substance does to someone: Han er påvirket af alkohol (He is under the influence of alcohol).

sentence.da: Dårlig søvn kan **påvirke** dit humør og din hukommelse.
sentence.en: Bad sleep can influence your mood and your memory.

en p-plads.explanation: "En p-plads" means "a parking spot". P stands for parkering (parking), and plads means space.

sentence.da: Hvert hus har en **p-plads** til bilen.
sentence.en: Every house has a parking spot for the car.

en p-skive.explanation: "En p-skive" means "a parking disc", a small cardboard dial you set to the time you arrived.

sentence.da: Husk at lægge en **p-skive** bag forruden.
sentence.en: Remember to put a parking disc behind the windshield.

en pakke.explanation: "En pakke" means "a package" or "a parcel", and also "a packet", like en pakke smør (a packet of butter).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **pakke** med posten i dag.
sentence.en: I got a package in the mail today.

en pakkeboks.explanation: "En pakkeboks" means "a parcel locker", a self-service box where you collect your parcel with a code.

sentence.da: Jeg henter pakken i en **pakkeboks** ved stationen.
sentence.en: I pick up the parcel from a parcel locker by the station.

en pakkekalender.explanation: "En pakkekalender" means "a gift Advent calendar", a calendar made of 24 small wrapped packages for the days up to December 24. It is a Danish tradition, and parents often make one at home for their children.

sentence.da: Børnene åbner en pakke i deres **pakkekalender** hver morgen i december.
sentence.en: The children open a package in their gift Advent calendar every morning in December.

en pakkeshop.explanation: "En pakkeshop" means "a parcel shop", an ordinary shop where you can also pick up and send parcels. Staff help you there, unlike at en pakkeboks (a parcel locker).

sentence.da: Jeg henter min pakke i en **pakkeshop** i dag.
sentence.en: I pick up my parcel at a parcel shop today.

en pande.explanation: "En pande" means "a pan", mostly a frying pan: Hun steger kødet på panden (She fries the meat in the pan). The same word also means "forehead": Han har ondt i panden (He has a pain in his forehead).

sentence.da: Jeg steger æg på en varm **pande**.
sentence.en: I fry eggs in a hot pan.

en pandekage.explanation: "En pandekage" means "a pancake", built from pande (a pan) and kage (a cake). Danes often eat them rolled up with jam or sugar.

sentence.da: Jeg steger en **pandekage** på en pande.
sentence.en: I fry a pancake in a pan.

en pandemi.explanation: "En pandemi" means "a pandemic", a disease that spreads across many countries at the same time, usually the whole world. A smaller one limited to one area is en epidemi (an epidemic).

sentence.da: Under en **pandemi** bliver mange skoler lukket, og folk arbejder hjemmefra.
sentence.en: During a pandemic many schools are closed, and people work from home.

en pantautomat.explanation: "En pantautomat" means "a bottle return machine". You put empty bottles and cans in it, and it prints a receipt. You may see a sign saying Pantautomaten er ude af drift (The machine is out of order).

sentence.da: Jeg afleverer tomme flasker i en **pantautomat**.
sentence.en: I return empty bottles in a bottle return machine.

en pantbon.explanation: "En pantbon" means "a deposit receipt". The machine prints it when you return bottles, and you hand it in at the checkout for money off your shopping.

sentence.da: Jeg afleverer min **pantbon** i kassen.
sentence.en: I hand in my deposit receipt at the checkout.

en papegøje.explanation: "En papegøje" means "a parrot", a colorful bird that can copy words.

sentence.da: Vores **papegøje** kan sige hej.
sentence.en: Our parrot can say hello.

en papirclips.explanation: "En papirclips" means "a paper clip", a small bent piece of wire that holds pages together. The word ends in s even for one clip and stays the same in the plural: to papirclips (two paper clips).

sentence.da: Jeg samler arkene med en **papirclips**, men du kan også bruge en hæftemaskine.
sentence.en: I put the sheets together with a paper clip, but you can also use a stapler.

en papirkurv.explanation: "En papirkurv" means "a wastepaper basket", a small bin for loose paper and other light waste, often placed by a desk.

sentence.da: Ved skrivebordet står en **papirkurv** til brugt papir.
sentence.en: By the desk there is a wastepaper basket for used paper.

en paraply.explanation: "En paraply" means "an umbrella", said pa-ra-PLY, with the stress on the last part.

sentence.da: Det regner, så jeg bruger en **paraply**.
sentence.en: It is raining, so I use an umbrella.

en parasol.explanation: "En parasol" means "a parasol", a large sunshade at a table or beach. For rain, use en paraply (an umbrella).

sentence.da: Vi sidder i skyggen under en **parasol**.
sentence.en: We sit in the shade under a parasol.

en parfume.explanation: "En parfume" means "a perfume", the liquid you put on your skin to smell nice.

sentence.da: Hun sprøjter **parfume** på halsen.
sentence.en: She sprays perfume on her neck.

en park.explanation: "En park" means "a park". You say i parken (in the park). Do not mix it up with at parkere (to park a car).

sentence.da: Vi går en tur i en **park**.
sentence.en: We go for a walk in a park.

en parkeringsautomat.explanation: "En parkeringsautomat" means "a parking meter", the machine where you pay to park.

sentence.da: Ved gaden står en **parkeringsautomat**, og den tager kun kort.
sentence.en: By the street there is a parking meter, and it only takes cards.

en parkeringsbøde.explanation: "En parkeringsbøde" means "a parking ticket", the fine you get for parking wrong: Du får en parkeringsbøde, hvis du holder for længe (You get a parking ticket if you park too long).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **parkeringsbøde** foran butikken.
sentence.en: I got a parking ticket in front of the shop.

en parkeringsplads.explanation: "En parkeringsplads" means "a parking space", and also "a parking lot", the whole area with many spaces. For short, Danes also say en p-plads (a parking spot).

sentence.da: Bilerne holder på en stor **parkeringsplads** ved butikken.
sentence.en: The cars are parked in a big parking lot by the store.

en parkeringsvagt.explanation: "En parkeringsvagt" means "a parking attendant", a person who checks parked cars and can give a ticket.

sentence.da: En **parkeringsvagt** går rundt og tjekker bilerne.
sentence.en: A parking attendant walks around and checks the cars.

en parodi.explanation: "En parodi" means "a parody", a funny copy that exaggerates something well known, such as a famous song, to make fun of it.

sentence.da: Filmen er en **parodi** på gamle gyserfilm og får alle til at grine.
sentence.en: The film is a parody of old horror films and makes everyone laugh.

en partner.explanation: "En partner" means "a partner", someone you share your life or business with. In a business, en partner is a co-owner.

sentence.da: Min **partner** og jeg bor i København.
sentence.en: My partner and I live in Copenhagen.

en passager.explanation: "En passager" means "a passenger", a person who travels in a car, train, plane or boat.

sentence.da: Hver **passager** skal have en billet.
sentence.en: Every passenger has to have a ticket.

en passagerfærge.explanation: "En passagerfærge" means "a passenger ferry", a boat that carries people. It is passager (passenger) plus færge (ferry). The same passager is in et passagerfly (a passenger plane).

sentence.da: Der sejler en **passagerfærge** til øen hver time.
sentence.en: A passenger ferry sails to the island every hour.

en pastor.explanation: "En pastor" means "a pastor", a minister who leads services and weddings. In Denmark the everyday word is en præst (a priest), and pastor is also used as a title before a name: pastor Hansen.

sentence.da: Vores **pastor** holder gudstjeneste hver søndag klokken ti.
sentence.en: Our pastor holds a service every Sunday at ten o'clock.

en patient.explanation: "En patient" means "a patient", a person getting medical care. Do not mix it up with the English word patient meaning calm: that is tålmodig in Danish.

sentence.da: Lægen hjælper en syg **patient** på sygehuset.
sentence.en: The doctor helps a sick patient at the hospital.

en patrulje.explanation: "En patrulje" means "a patrol", a small group that walks or drives around an area to watch over it, such as soldiers or police.

sentence.da: En **patrulje** går rundt i området hver nat og holder øje med folk.
sentence.en: A patrol walks around the area every night and keeps an eye on people.

en pause.explanation: "En pause" means "a break" or "a pause", for example at work or school. At holde pause means "to take a break", and a coffee break is en kaffepause.

sentence.da: Nu holder vi **pause** og drikker kaffe.
sentence.en: Now we take a break and drink coffee.

en pave.explanation: "En pave" means "a pope", the leader of the Catholic Church.

sentence.da: Katolikkerne har en **pave**, som bor i Rom.
sentence.en: Catholics have a pope, who lives in Rome.

en peberfrugt.explanation: "En peberfrugt" means "a bell pepper", the colorful vegetable you slice for salads. Peber (pepper) alone is the spice.

sentence.da: En rød **peberfrugt** smager sødt og er ikke stærk.
sentence.en: A red bell pepper tastes sweet and is not hot.

en peberkværn.explanation: "En peberkværn" means "a pepper mill", which grinds whole peppercorns fresh over your food: Drej peberkværnen to gange (Turn the pepper mill twice).

sentence.da: Hun maler frisk peber med en **peberkværn**.
sentence.en: She grinds fresh pepper with a pepper mill.

en pebernød.explanation: "En pebernød" means "a small Christmas spice cookie". It is built from peber (pepper) and nød (nut), but it has no nuts: Vi spiser pebernødder i julen (We eat spice cookies at Christmas).

sentence.da: Til jul spiser jeg en **pebernød** eller to.
sentence.en: At Christmas I eat a spice cookie or two.

en pegefinger.explanation: "En pegefinger" means "an index finger", the finger you point with. The first part is at pege (to point), as in en pegepind (a pointer stick).

sentence.da: Du bruger din **pegefinger**, når du peger på noget.
sentence.en: You use your index finger when you point at something.

en pels.explanation: "En pels" means "a fur", a warm garment made from animal skin with the hair left on. It is also the word for the fur on a living animal: hundens pels (the dog's fur).

sentence.da: En **pels** er lavet af dyrehuder og holder dig varm.
sentence.en: A fur is made of animal skins and keeps you warm.

en pen.explanation: "En pen" means "a pen". Do not mix it up with pæn (nice, pretty), which is spelled with an æ.

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mit navn med en **pen**.
sentence.en: I write my name with a pen.

en pendler.explanation: "En pendler" means "a commuter", a person who travels between home and work every day, often a long way.

sentence.da: Som **pendler** tager hun toget til arbejde hver dag.
sentence.en: As a commuter she takes the train to work every day.

en pengepung.explanation: "En pengepung" means "a purse", a small case for coins, bills and cards. For the bag you carry on your shoulder (what Americans call a purse), say en håndtaske (a handbag), not pengepung.

sentence.da: Jeg har kun en lille mønt i min **pengepung**.
sentence.en: I only have a small coin in my purse.

en pensel.explanation: "En pensel" means "a paintbrush": Kan jeg låne en pensel? (Can I borrow a paintbrush?) A brush for teeth or cleaning is en børste (a brush): en tandbørste (a toothbrush).

sentence.da: Hun maler et billede med en tynd **pensel**.
sentence.en: She paints a picture with a thin paintbrush.

en pension.explanation: "En pension" means "a pension", money you get every month after you stop working. The word also names that time of life: Min far går på pension i år (My father retires this year).

sentence.da: Efter mange år på arbejde får hun nu en **pension**.
sentence.en: After many years at work, she now gets a pension.

en pensionist.explanation: "En pensionist" means "a retiree", a person who has stopped working and gets money from the state or a pension fund: Min farfar er pensionist (My grandfather is a retiree).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **pensionist** og arbejder ikke mere.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a retiree and doesn't work anymore.

en periode.explanation: "En periode" means "a period" of time: en lang periode (a long period) and i en periode (for a while). The dot at the end of a sentence is not this word; that is et punktum (a period).

sentence.da: Jeg har haft en travl **periode** på arbejdet.
sentence.en: I have had a busy period at work.

en perron.explanation: "En perron" means "a platform" at a train station. You say på perronen (on the platform).

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget på **perron** to.
sentence.en: We wait for the train on platform two.

en persienne.explanation: "En persienne" means "a blind", the kind with flat slats that you tilt or pull up: Luk persiennen, så det bliver mørkt (Close the blind so it gets dark).

sentence.da: Soveværelset har en **persienne** mod solen.
sentence.en: The bedroom has a blind against the sun.

en person.explanation: "En person" means "a person". When booking, you say et bord til to personer (a table for two people).

sentence.da: Billetten gælder for én **person**.
sentence.en: The ticket is valid for one person.

en personlig træner.explanation: "En personlig træner" means "a personal trainer", a person you pay to plan your workouts and help you exercise. A træner (coach) of a team works with many people at once.

sentence.da: Jeg har en **personlig træner**, som laver mit træningsprogram.
sentence.en: I have a personal trainer who makes my training program.

en personlighed.explanation: "En personlighed" means "a personality", the way a person is: Hun har en varm personlighed (She has a warm personality). It can also mean a well-known person: en kendt personlighed (a well-known figure).

sentence.da: Humor er en vigtig del af hans **personlighed**.
sentence.en: Humor is an important part of his personality.

en pest.explanation: "En pest" means "a plague", a deadly disease that killed millions of people in Europe in the Middle Ages. It also works in an idiom: Jeg undgår ham som pesten (I avoid him like the plague).

sentence.da: En **pest** er en meget farlig sygdom, som smitter hurtigt.
sentence.en: A plague is a very dangerous disease that spreads quickly.

en ph.d..explanation: "En ph.d." means "a PhD", the highest degree at a university, usually after about three years of study beyond a master's degree. In Denmark it is usually a paid job at a university.

sentence.da: Hun er i gang med en **ph.d.** om børns sprog.
sentence.en: She is working on a PhD about children's language.

en picnic.explanation: "En picnic" means "a picnic", a meal outdoors. To go on one, say at tage på picnic (to go on a picnic).

sentence.da: Vi tager på **picnic** i parken, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: We go on a picnic in the park when it is warm.

en pige.explanation: "En pige" means "a girl", a child or teenager: En pige på ti år (A ten-year-old girl). For a grown woman, say en kvinde (a woman).

sentence.da: En **pige** og en dreng leger i haven.
sentence.en: A girl and a boy play in the garden.

en pil.explanation: "En pil" means "an arrow", the pointed sign or the kind shot from a bow, and also "a willow", the tree. For the tree you can also say et piletræ (a willow tree).

sentence.da: Skiltet har en **pil**, der peger til højre.
sentence.en: The sign has an arrow that points to the right.

en pille.explanation: "En pille" means "a pill" or "a tablet". You say at tage en pille (to take a pill). Pillen (the pill) can also mean the birth control pill.

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt og tager en **pille**.
sentence.en: I am in pain and take a pill.

en pilot.explanation: "En pilot" means "a pilot", the person who flies a plane. The word is the same for men and women: Hun er pilot (She is a pilot).

sentence.da: Min onkel er **pilot** og flyver til Asien.
sentence.en: My uncle is a pilot and flies to Asia.

en pind.explanation: "En pind" means "a stick", a small thin piece of wood: Drengen tegner med en pind i sandet (The boy draws in the sand with a stick).

sentence.da: Hunden løber efter en **pind**.
sentence.en: The dog runs after a stick.

en pingvin.explanation: "En pingvin" means "a penguin", the black and white sea bird that cannot fly.

sentence.da: En **pingvin** er en fugl, der svømmer.
sentence.en: A penguin is a bird that swims.

en pinkode.explanation: "En pinkode" means "a PIN code", the secret number for your bank card: Jeg har glemt min pinkode (I have forgotten my PIN code).

sentence.da: Tast din **pinkode** ved kassen.
sentence.en: Enter your PIN code at the checkout.

en pirat.explanation: "En pirat" means "a pirate", a robber at sea. Piracy of films and music is called piratkopiering (pirated copying).

sentence.da: Den onde **pirat** sejler over havet.
sentence.en: The evil pirate sails across the sea.

en pistol.explanation: "En pistol" means "a pistol" or "a gun", a small gun held in one hand: Politiet fandt en pistol i bilen (The police found a pistol in the car).

sentence.da: Han havde en **pistol** i lommen.
sentence.en: He had a pistol in his pocket.

en pita.explanation: "En pita" means "a pita", a round flatbread with a pocket inside for filling: Jeg spiser en pita med falafel (I eat a pita with falafel).

sentence.da: Jeg fylder en **pita** med salat og kylling.
sentence.en: I fill a pita with salad and chicken.

en pizza.explanation: "En pizza" means "a pizza". To order one to take away, say en pizza til at tage med (a pizza to take with you).

sentence.da: En **pizza** har bund, sauce og ost.
sentence.en: A pizza has a base, sauce and cheese.

en pizzeria.explanation: "En pizzeria" means "a pizzeria", a casual restaurant that sells pizza: Vi spiser på den lille pizzeria (We eat at the little pizzeria).

sentence.da: Vi spiser pizza på en lille **pizzeria**.
sentence.en: We eat pizza at a small pizzeria.

en plade.explanation: "En plade" means "a plate" in the sense of a flat piece of metal, wood or stone: en plade af træ (a wooden board). It also means "a record": Jeg køber en gammel plade (I buy an old record). A dinner plate is en tallerken (a plate).

sentence.da: Han lytter til en gammel **plade**.
sentence.en: He listens to an old record.

en pladespiller.explanation: "En pladespiller" means "a record player", a machine that plays music from round vinyl discs. A disc like that is called en plade (a record).

sentence.da: På en **pladespiller** kan man høre musik fra sorte vinylplader.
sentence.en: On a record player you can hear music from black vinyl records.

en plads.explanation: "En plads" means "a seat", "room (space)" or "a town square". On a train or in a cinema, en plads is your seat. Er der plads? means "Is there room?".

forms.en: the seat / the room / the square

sentence.da: Der er ikke **plads** i bussen.
sentence.en: There is no room on the bus.

en plaid.explanation: "En plaid" means "a throw blanket", a soft blanket for the sofa: Jeg sidder med en plaid over benene (I sit with a throw blanket over my legs).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder i sofaen med en varm **plaid**.
sentence.en: I sit on the sofa with a warm throw blanket.

en plakat.explanation: "En plakat" means "a poster", on a wall or a board: Der hænger en plakat på væggen (A poster hangs on the wall).

sentence.da: Jeg har hængt en **plakat** op i mit værelse.
sentence.en: I have hung a poster up in my room.

en plan.explanation: "En plan" means "a plan". You can ask Har du planer i weekenden? (Do you have plans this weekend?). En køreplan (a timetable) is a plan for trains and buses.

sentence.da: Vores **plan** er at tage toget.
sentence.en: Our plan is to take the train.

en planet.explanation: "En planet" means "a planet". It is also used for the whole world: Vi skal passe på planeten (We must take care of the planet).

sentence.da: Mars er en rød **planet**.
sentence.en: Mars is a red planet.

en planke.explanation: "En planke" means "a plank", a long, flat, thick piece of wood used to build floors, fences and docks. Planker (planks) are often laid side by side.

sentence.da: Hvert stykke i gulvet er en **planke**.
sentence.en: Each piece in the floor is a plank.

en plante.explanation: "En plante" means "a plant", something that grows in soil: Jeg vander planterne hver dag (I water the plants every day). The same word also works as at plante (to plant): Vi planter et træ (We plant a tree).

sentence.da: Min **plante** har brug for mere lys.
sentence.en: My plant needs more light.

en planteskole.explanation: "En planteskole" means "a plant nursery", a place where young plants and trees are grown and sold. It is not a place for small children: a daycare for babies is en vuggestue.

sentence.da: På en **planteskole** kan man købe unge træer og buske til haven.
sentence.en: At a plant nursery you can buy young trees and bushes for the garden.

en plastikpose.explanation: "En plastikpose" means "a plastic bag", from plastik (plastic) and en pose (a bag). In shops, you may hear Vil du have en pose? (Do you want a bag?).

sentence.da: Jeg har æbler i en **plastikpose**.
sentence.en: I have apples in a plastic bag.

en platform.explanation: "En platform" means "a platform", mostly an online place where people share, watch or buy things. At a train station the platform is en perron (a station platform), not en platform.

sentence.da: Instagram er en **platform**, hvor man deler billeder med venner.
sentence.en: Instagram is a platform where you share pictures with friends.

en playliste.explanation: "En playliste" means "a playlist", a list of songs you pick yourself: Jeg har en playliste til bilen (I have a playlist for the car).

sentence.da: Jeg lytter til min **playliste**, når jeg løber.
sentence.en: I listen to my playlist when I run.

en plejefamilie.explanation: "En plejefamilie" means "a foster family", a family that takes in a child who cannot live with their own parents, for a short time or for many years. In Denmark the municipality (kommunen) decides when a child is placed in one.

sentence.da: Barnet bor hos en **plejefamilie**, fordi forældrene ikke kan tage sig af det.
sentence.en: The child lives with a foster family because the parents cannot take care of it.

en plet.explanation: "En plet" means "a stain" or "a spot", a mark that does not belong: Der er en plet på min skjorte (There is a stain on my shirt). It can also be a small area: en grøn plet (a green spot).

sentence.da: Der er en **plet** på min nye skjorte.
sentence.en: There is a stain on my new shirt.

en pligt.explanation: "En pligt" means "a duty", something you must do: Det er din pligt at hjælpe (It is your duty to help). A well-known saying is Pligt før fornøjelse (Duty before pleasure).

sentence.da: Det er hans **pligt** at passe på børnene.
sentence.en: It is his duty to take care of the children.

en pligtfølelse.explanation: "En pligtfølelse" means "a sense of duty", the feeling that you must do something because it is right or expected, even when you do not want to.

sentence.da: Af **pligtfølelse** passede hun sin syge mor hver dag.
sentence.en: Out of a sense of duty, she looked after her sick mother every day.

en plov.explanation: "En plov" means "a plow", a farm tool that cuts and turns over the soil before seeds are planted. Today a tractor pulls it; long ago, horses or oxen did.

sentence.da: Landmanden bruger en **plov** til at vende jorden.
sentence.en: The farmer uses a plow to turn the soil.

en plæne.explanation: "En plæne" means "a lawn", the grass area by a house: Børnene leger på plænen (The children play on the lawn). Græs (grass) is the plant itself, and plæne is the whole area.

sentence.da: Vi spiser frokost på en grøn **plæne**.
sentence.en: We eat lunch on a green lawn.

en podcast.explanation: "En podcast" means "a podcast", a show you listen to online: Jeg hører en podcast om historie (I am listening to a podcast about history).

sentence.da: Jeg hører en **podcast**, når jeg cykler på arbejde.
sentence.en: I listen to a podcast when I bike to work.

en pointe.explanation: "En pointe" means "a point", the main idea of a story or an argument, the thing that makes it worth telling. A score in a game is et point (a point), not en pointe.

sentence.da: Jeg forstod ikke hans **pointe**, før han forklarede det.
sentence.en: I did not understand his point until he explained it.

en pokal.explanation: "En pokal" means "a trophy", often shaped like a cup, that a team or person gets for winning a competition.

sentence.da: Holdet fik en stor **pokal**, fordi det vandt finalen.
sentence.en: The team got a big trophy because it won the final.

en polak.explanation: "En polak" means "a Pole", a person from Poland: Min nabo er polak (My neighbor is Polish). For things from Poland, use polsk: polsk pølse (Polish sausage).

sentence.da: En **polak** kommer fra Polen.
sentence.en: A Pole comes from Poland.

en politibetjent.explanation: "En politibetjent" means "a police officer": Politibetjenten viste os vej (The police officer showed us the way). It is the neutral word for a man or a woman.

sentence.da: Du kan bede en **politibetjent** om hjælp.
sentence.en: You can ask a police officer for help.

en politik.explanation: "En politik" means "a policy", the rules a group follows: Skolens politik er klar (The school's policy is clear). Without en, politik also means "politics": Han taler om politik (He talks about politics).

sentence.da: Skolen har en klar **politik** mod mobning.
sentence.en: The school has a clear policy against bullying.

en politiker.explanation: "En politiker" means "a politician", a person with a job in politics, in a city or for the whole country: Hun er blevet politiker (She has become a politician). The field itself is politik (politics).

sentence.da: En **politiker** stemmer om love i Folketinget.
sentence.en: A politician votes on laws in the Parliament.

en politimand.explanation: "En politimand" means "a policeman". The whole force is politiet (the police): Politiet kommer (The police are coming). For a word that fits men and women, say en politibetjent (a police officer).

sentence.da: Jeg spurgte en **politimand** om vej.
sentence.en: I asked a policeman for directions.

en politistation.explanation: "En politistation" means "a police station", built from politi (police) and station (station). You say på politistationen (at the police station).

sentence.da: Politibetjenten arbejder på en **politistation**.
sentence.en: The police officer works at a police station.

en pollenallergi.explanation: "En pollenallergi" means "a pollen allergy", a reaction to the fine dust from flowers and trees. It gives itchy eyes and a runny nose, mostly in spring and summer.

sentence.da: Med **pollenallergi** er det svært at være ude, når birken blomstrer.
sentence.en: With a pollen allergy it is hard to be outside when the birch tree blooms.

en polo.explanation: "En polo" means "a polo shirt", the short-sleeved shirt with a collar and a few buttons: Han har en hvid polo på (He is wearing a white polo shirt).

sentence.da: Han har en hvid **polo** på til festen.
sentence.en: He is wearing a white polo shirt to the party.

en polterabend.explanation: "En polterabend" means "a pre-wedding party", a party with friends for a couple just before they marry. Friends often smash old plates outside the door, because broken pieces are said to bring luck.

sentence.da: Aftenen før brylluppet holder vennerne en **polterabend** for brudeparret.
sentence.en: The evening before the wedding, the friends hold a pre-wedding party for the bridal couple.

en pony.explanation: "En pony" means "a pony", a small horse that children often ride: Barnet rider på en pony (The child rides a pony). A full-size horse is en hest (a horse).

sentence.da: Min datter rider på en **pony** hver lørdag.
sentence.en: My daughter rides a pony every Saturday.

en pool.explanation: "En pool" means "a pool" for swimming, often in a garden or at a hotel: Poolen er varm i dag (The pool is warm today). For a big public pool building, say en svømmehal (a swimming hall).

sentence.da: Vi har en lille **pool** i haven.
sentence.en: We have a small pool in the garden.

en porre.explanation: "En porre" means "a leek", a long vegetable that is white at the bottom and green at the top. It tastes like a mild onion.

sentence.da: Jeg laver suppe med **porre** og kartofler.
sentence.en: I make soup with leek and potatoes.

en port.explanation: "En port" means "a gate", like the gate to a yard or a farm: Porten er åben (The gate is open). A small garden gate is en låge (a small gate).

sentence.da: Gården har en stor **port** til bilerne.
sentence.en: The yard has a big gate for the cars.

en portion.explanation: "En portion" means "a portion" or "a serving", such as one person's share of food. In restaurants, you may hear en lille portion (a small portion) or en stor portion (a large one).

sentence.da: Én **portion** er nok til en person.
sentence.en: One portion is enough for one person.

en pose.explanation: "En pose" means "a bag", a soft bag made of plastic or paper. A bag you carry, such as a handbag, is en taske (a bag, purse).

sentence.da: Jeg lagde æblerne i en **pose** af papir.
sentence.en: I put the apples in a paper bag.

en position.explanation: "En position" means "a position": where something stands in a ranking, on a map or on a team.

sentence.da: Hvilken **position** spiller du på holdet?
sentence.en: Which position do you play on the team?

en postkasse.explanation: "En postkasse" means "a mailbox", the box by your door or on the street. It is built from post (mail) and kasse (box). Kasse also means the checkout in a store: Jeg betaler ved kassen (I pay at the checkout).

sentence.da: Postbuddet lægger breve i vores **postkasse**.
sentence.en: The mail carrier puts letters in our mailbox.

en pote.explanation: "En pote" means "a paw", the foot of a dog, cat or bear. A well-known command to a dog is Giv pote! (Shake!).

sentence.da: Hunden har ondt i en **pote** og halter.
sentence.en: The dog has a sore paw and limps.

en potte.explanation: "En potte" means "a pot" for a plant. Small children also sit on en potte (a potty) when they learn to use the toilet.

sentence.da: Jeg har sat basilikum i en **potte** på vindueskarmen.
sentence.en: I have put basil in a pot on the windowsill.

en potteplante.explanation: "En potteplante" means "a houseplant", a plant that grows in a pot indoors.

sentence.da: Min **potteplante** står i en pot og skal have vand.
sentence.en: My houseplant stands in a pot and needs water.

en praksis.explanation: "En praksis" means "a practice", the way something is really done, as opposed to what is only planned. A doctor's office is called en lægepraksis (a doctor's practice).

sentence.da: Jeg har lært teorien, men jeg mangler **praksis**.
sentence.en: I have learned the theory, but I lack practice.

en praktikant.explanation: "En praktikant" means "an intern", someone who works at a company for a limited time to learn the job, often as part of a study program.

sentence.da: Som **praktikant** lærer man jobbet ved at hjælpe de andre.
sentence.en: As an intern you learn the job by helping the others.

en praktikplads.explanation: "En praktikplads" means "an internship placement", a spot at a company where you do the practical part of your studies. In Denmark, students in trade programs must find one to finish.

sentence.da: Jeg skal have en **praktikplads**, før jeg kan blive færdig med uddannelsen.
sentence.en: I need an internship placement before I can finish my education.

en praktiserende læge.explanation: "En praktiserende læge" means "a general practitioner", the doctor you go to first for most health problems and who can send you on for more tests. Many people just say min læge (my doctor).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til min **praktiserende læge**, hvis jeg bliver syg.
sentence.en: I call my general practitioner if I get sick.

en premiere.explanation: "En premiere" means "a premiere", the first public showing of a film or a play. To say something opens, use har premiere: Filmen har premiere i morgen (The film opens tomorrow).

sentence.da: I aften er der **premiere** på det nye teaterstykke.
sentence.en: Tonight there is a premiere of the new play.

en presse.explanation: "En presse" means "a press", mostly the reporters and TV and radio stations as a group: Pressen skriver om det (The press is writing about it). It is also a machine that squeezes things.

sentence.da: Der var meget **presse** til stede, da ministeren kom.
sentence.en: There was a lot of press present when the minister arrived.

en prik.explanation: "En prik" means "a dot", a small round mark. Something covered in dots is prikket (dotted), like a dress with polka dots.

sentence.da: Tegn en **prik** med pennen, ikke en streg.
sentence.en: Draw a dot with the pen, not a line.

en prins.explanation: "En prins" means "a prince", a royal son. In a title, it comes before the name: Prins Joachim er kongens bror (Prince Joachim is the king's brother).

sentence.da: En **prins** er søn af en konge.
sentence.en: A prince is the son of a king.

en prinsesse.explanation: "En prinsesse" means "a princess", the daughter of a king or queen.

sentence.da: Hun har en krone på og ligner en **prinsesse**.
sentence.en: She has a crown on and looks like a princess.

en printer.explanation: "En printer" means "a printer", the machine that prints on paper.

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge en **printer** til at printe dokumentet.
sentence.en: I need a printer to print the document.

en prioritering.explanation: "En prioritering" means "a prioritization", the choice of what comes first and what must wait. It is common in work, politics and budgets, where not everything can be done at once.

sentence.da: Med så få penge er en klar **prioritering** nødvendig.
sentence.en: With so little money, a clear prioritization is necessary.

en prioritet.explanation: "En prioritet" means "a priority", what you decide matters most and do first. The verb at prioritere (to prioritize) means to choose what to put first.

sentence.da: Min families trivsel er min højeste **prioritet** lige nu.
sentence.en: My family's well-being is my highest priority right now.

en pris.explanation: "En pris" means "a price", what something costs. The same word also means a prize or award, so the situation tells you which: en pris på tyve kroner (a price of twenty crowns) is a price, while at vinde en pris (to win a prize) is an award.

sentence.da: Den lave **pris** gør varen billig.
sentence.en: The low price makes the item cheap.

en prisforskel.explanation: "En prisforskel" means "a price difference", how much more one thing costs than another. It is built from pris (price) and forskel (difference). Forskel also appears in Det gør ingen forskel (It makes no difference).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **prisforskel** mellem butikkerne.
sentence.en: There is a big price difference between the stores.

en prisstigning.explanation: "En prisstigning" means "a price increase", when something costs more than before. It can be a rise for one product or for most prices in a country at once.

sentence.da: Der kommer en **prisstigning** på mælk fra næste måned.
sentence.en: There is a price increase on milk from next month.

en privatperson.explanation: "En privatperson" means "a private individual", a person acting for themselves, not for a company or an authority. Rules and prices are often different for privatpersoner (private individuals) and for firms.

sentence.da: Banken har andre regler for en **privatperson** end for et firma.
sentence.en: The bank has other rules for a private individual than for a firm.

en problemstilling.explanation: "En problemstilling" means "an issue to address", the specific matter that a project, report or school assignment sets out to look into and solve.

sentence.da: I opgaven undersøger vi en **problemstilling** om unges søvn.
sentence.en: In the assignment, we investigate an issue about young people's sleep.

en procedure.explanation: "En procedure" means "a procedure", a fixed way of doing something: Vi følger en procedure (We follow a procedure). For something that changes over time, use proces: Det er en lang proces (It is a long process).

sentence.da: Der er en fast **procedure** for nye kunder.
sentence.en: There is a set procedure for new customers.

en procent.explanation: "En procent" means "a percent". With a number it stays procent: tre procent (three percent).

sentence.da: Kun fem **procent** af eleverne er syge.
sentence.en: Only five percent of the students are sick.

en proces.explanation: "En proces" means "a process", a series of changes over time. A fixed set of rules for doing something is en procedure (a procedure).

sentence.da: At lære et sprog er en langsom **proces**.
sentence.en: Learning a language is a slow process.

en producer.explanation: "En producer" means "a producer" of a film, TV show or music. For a company that makes goods, Danes say en producent (a manufacturer).

sentence.da: Min ven er **producer** og laver film.
sentence.en: My friend is a producer and makes films.

en professor.explanation: "En professor" means "a professor", a senior teacher at a university. A teacher at a normal school is en lærer (a teacher).

sentence.da: En **professor** underviser på et universitet.
sentence.en: A professor teaches at a university.

en profil.explanation: "En profil" means "a profile", your own page with your name and photo on a website or app. It can also mean a side view of a face: Fotoet viser hende i profil (The photo shows her in profile).

sentence.da: Jeg har skrevet lidt om mig selv på min **profil**.
sentence.en: I wrote a little about myself on my profile.

en programmør.explanation: "En programmør" means "a programmer", someone who writes computer code: Programmøren arbejder hjemmefra (The programmer works from home). The word is the same for men and women.

sentence.da: En **programmør** skriver kode til computere.
sentence.en: A programmer writes code for computers.

en projektleder.explanation: "En projektleder" means "a project manager", the person who plans a project, divides the work and makes sure it is finished on time.

sentence.da: Hun er **projektleder** og sørger for, at alle når deres frister.
sentence.en: She is a project manager and makes sure everyone meets their deadlines.

en proptrækker.explanation: "En proptrækker" means "a corkscrew". It is built from prop (cork) and trække (to pull), so it pulls the cork out. Prop also means a plug, as in en trafikprop (a traffic jam).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke åbne vinen uden en **proptrækker**.
sentence.en: I cannot open the wine without a corkscrew.

en protest.explanation: "En protest" means "a protest", a public way of showing that you disagree with a decision. It can be a big march in the street or just a letter.

sentence.da: Mange gik på gaden i **protest** mod de nye regler.
sentence.en: Many went into the street in protest against the new rules.

en præmie.explanation: "En præmie" means "a prize", something you get for winning. It also means the amount you pay for insurance (a premium): Præmien er tusind kroner om året (The premium is a thousand kroner a year).

sentence.da: Vinderen af konkurrencen får en stor **præmie**.
sentence.en: The winner of the contest gets a big prize.

en præsentation.explanation: "En præsentation" means "a presentation", a spoken show with slides. The usual verb is at holde (to hold): Chefen holder en præsentation (The boss gives a presentation).

sentence.da: Jeg skal holde en **præsentation** på mandag.
sentence.en: I am going to give a presentation on Monday.

en præsident.explanation: "En præsident" means "a president", the head of a country, or of a club or an organization.

sentence.da: En **præsident** leder et land.
sentence.en: A president leads a country.

en præst.explanation: "En præst" means "a priest", and in Denmark it is also the normal word for a church minister. It is used for both men and women.

sentence.da: Vores **præst** holder en tale i kirken.
sentence.en: Our priest gives a speech in church.

en præstation.explanation: "En præstation" means "a performance", how well someone does or what they achieve in sports, at work or at school. A show on a stage is en forestilling (a show), not en præstation.

sentence.da: Han leverede en flot **præstation** og vandt løbet.
sentence.en: He delivered a fine performance and won the race.

en prøve.explanation: "En prøve" means "a test" or "a quiz": Vi har en prøve i matematik (We have a test in math). It also means "a sample", as in en prøve af osten (a sample of the cheese).

sentence.da: Vi skriver en **prøve** i geografi på fredag.
sentence.en: We are taking a test in geography on Friday.

en prøvetid.explanation: "En prøvetid" means "a probation period", the first weeks or months of a new job, when either side can end it quickly. During it, both sides test whether the job suits them.

sentence.da: En ny medarbejder har en **prøvetid** på tre måneder.
sentence.en: A new employee has a probation period of three months.

en psykiater.explanation: "En psykiater" means "a psychiatrist". Do not mix it up with en psykolog (a psychologist): a psychiatrist is a medical doctor who can prescribe medicine, and a psychologist is not.

sentence.da: En **psykiater** taler med patienter om deres tanker og følelser.
sentence.en: A psychiatrist talks with patients about their thoughts and feelings.

en psykolog.explanation: "En psykolog" means "a psychologist", someone you talk to about feelings and worries: Jeg skal til psykolog (I am going to see a psychologist). A psykiater (psychiatrist) is a medical doctor who can also prescribe medicine.

sentence.da: Hun taler med en **psykolog** om sine bekymringer.
sentence.en: She talks to a psychologist about her worries.

en psykopat.explanation: "En psykopat" means "a psychopath", a person who feels no sympathy and does not care about hurting others. In everyday speech it is also used loosely and sounds harsh: Han kørte som en psykopat (He drove like a maniac).

sentence.da: Krimien handler om en **psykopat**, som dræber uden at fortryde det.
sentence.en: The crime novel is about a psychopath who kills without regret.

en publikation.explanation: "En publikation" means "a publication", a text that has been officially published, such as a book, a report or a scientific paper. Do not mix it up with publikum (an audience), which looks similar.

sentence.da: Forskerne udgav en **publikation** om børns søvn.
sentence.en: The researchers released a publication about children's sleep.

en pude.explanation: "En pude" means "a pillow" or "a cushion", for example on a sofa. A bed pillow can be called en hovedpude (literally a head pillow).

sentence.da: Mit hoved ligger på en blød **pude**.
sentence.en: My head lies on a soft pillow.

en puls.explanation: "En puls" means "a pulse", the beat of your heart that you can feel on your wrist or neck. In everyday Danish the word is also used for how fast the heart beats.

sentence.da: Efter løbeturen er min **puls** høj, og jeg er forpustet.
sentence.en: After the run my pulse is high and I am out of breath.

en pung.explanation: "En pung" means "a wallet". En tegnebog (a wallet) means the same, but pung is the everyday word.

sentence.da: Mine penge er i min **pung**.
sentence.en: My money is in my wallet.

en punktering.explanation: "En punktering" means "a flat tire" or "a puncture", a hole in a bike or car tire that lets the air out.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke cykle, fordi jeg har en **punktering**.
sentence.en: I can't bike because I have a flat tire.

en pyjamas.explanation: "En pyjamas" means "a pair of pajamas". Danish treats it as one thing, so you say en pyjamas (literally a pajamas) where English says a pair of pajamas.

sentence.da: Jeg har min **pyjamas** på i sengen.
sentence.en: I am wearing my pajamas in bed.

en pyt.explanation: "En pyt" means "a puddle", a small amount of water lying on the ground after rain. The same spelling is also the very common Danish word Pyt! (Never mind!), but that one has no en in front.

sentence.da: Der er en stor **pyt** midt på vejen.
sentence.en: There is a big puddle in the middle of the road.

en påskeferie.explanation: "En påskeferie" means "an Easter vacation", the days off around Easter. Schools in Denmark close at that time, and many families travel.

sentence.da: Skolen holder lukket i en uges **påskeferie**.
sentence.en: The school is closed for a week of Easter vacation.

en påskefrokost.explanation: "En påskefrokost" means "an Easter lunch", a long lunch with family or friends, like a julefrokost (a Christmas lunch) but in spring. A special beer, påskebryg (Easter beer), is sold for it.

sentence.da: Hele familien samles til en lang **påskefrokost** med sild og æg.
sentence.en: The whole family gathers for a long Easter lunch with herring and eggs.

en påstand.explanation: "En påstand" means "a claim", something said to be true, often without anything to back it up. When you call something en påstand, you often doubt it: Det er kun en påstand (It is only a claim).

sentence.da: Hun kan ikke bevise sin **påstand**, så ingen tror på den.
sentence.en: She cannot prove her claim, so nobody believes it.

en påvirkning.explanation: "En påvirkning" means "an influence", the way something changes how a person or thing acts or feels. It is also used for being drunk: kørsel under påvirkning (driving under the influence).

sentence.da: Skærme har en stor **påvirkning** af børns søvn.
sentence.en: Screens have a big influence on children's sleep.

en pædagog.explanation: "En pædagog" means "a daycare worker", someone who looks after and teaches children and young people outside of school.

sentence.da: En **pædagog** passer børn i en børnehave.
sentence.en: A daycare worker looks after children in a kindergarten.

en pære.explanation: "En pære" means "a pear" and also "a light bulb", so the situation tells you which one is meant: en saftig pære (a juicy pear) is fruit, while en ny pære til lampen (a new bulb for the lamp) is a light bulb.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en sød **pære** og et æble.
sentence.en: I eat a sweet pear and an apple.

en pølse.explanation: "En pølse" means "a sausage". In Danish, a hot dog is en hotdog or en pølse i brød (a sausage in bread), and a street stand that sells them is en pølsevogn (a hot dog cart).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en varm **pølse** med brød.
sentence.en: I eat a hot sausage with bread.

en pølsevogn.explanation: "En pølsevogn" means "a hot dog stand", a small food wagon on the street that sells hot dogs. It is built from pølse (sausage) and vogn (wagon). Vogn is also in en indkøbsvogn (a shopping cart) and en barnevogn (a stroller).

sentence.da: Hun sælger varme pølser fra en **pølsevogn**.
sentence.en: She sells hot dogs from a hot dog stand.

et palads.explanation: "Et palads" means "a palace", a very large, grand building where a ruler lives. Danish also has et slot (a castle), which is the usual word for royal homes like Amalienborg Slot.

sentence.da: Et **palads** har mange store sale og en stor have.
sentence.en: A palace has many big halls and a big garden.

et par.explanation: "Et par" means "a pair" or "a couple", as in et par sko (a pair of shoes). It also means "a few": et par dage means "a couple of days". Two people in a relationship are also et par (a couple).

sentence.da: Jeg bliver her et **par** dage.
sentence.en: I will stay here for a couple of days.

et par jeans.explanation: "Et par jeans" means "a pair of jeans". You can also just say jeans: Jeg har jeans på means "I am wearing jeans".

sentence.da: Jeg køber et **par jeans** i dag.
sentence.en: I am buying a pair of jeans today.

et paradis.explanation: "Et paradis" means "a paradise", a perfect place of happiness. In religion, it is where good people go after death. In everyday speech, it is any wonderful place: Stranden er et paradis for børn (The beach is a paradise for children).

sentence.da: Øen er et **paradis** med hvide strande og blåt vand.
sentence.en: The island is a paradise with white beaches and blue water.

et paraplystativ.explanation: "Et paraplystativ" means "an umbrella stand", a holder by the door for wet umbrellas. It is built from paraply (umbrella) and stativ (stand).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter den våde paraply i et **paraplystativ**.
sentence.en: I put the wet umbrella in an umbrella stand.

et parkeringshus.explanation: "Et parkeringshus" means "a parking garage", a building with several floors for cars. It is built from at parkere (to park) and et hus (a house).

sentence.da: Der er ingen pladser på gaden, men der er et **parkeringshus**.
sentence.en: There are no spaces on the street, but there is a parking garage.

et parti.explanation: "Et parti" means "a political party", a group with shared political goals that runs in elections. It also means one game of chess or cards: Vi spiller et parti skak (We are playing a game of chess). For a party with food and music, use en fest (a party).

sentence.da: Socialdemokratiet er et stort **parti** i Danmark.
sentence.en: The Social Democrats are a big party in Denmark.

et pas.explanation: "Et pas" means "a passport", the document you show at the border. Husk dit pas means "Remember your passport". Do not mix it up with at passe (to fit, to look after), which looks similar.

sentence.da: Ved grænsen skal du vise dit **pas**.
sentence.en: At the border you must show your passport.

et pasfoto.explanation: "Et pasfoto" means "a passport photo", a small picture for your passport or ID. It is built from pas (passport) and foto (photo).

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge et nyt **pasfoto** til mit pas.
sentence.en: I need a new passport photo for my passport.

et penalhus.explanation: "Et penalhus" means "a pencil case", a small case for pens and pencils at school.

sentence.da: Min kuglepen ligger i mit **penalhus**.
sentence.en: My pen is in my pencil case.

et pengeskab.explanation: "Et pengeskab" means "a safe", a strong locked box for money, passports and other valuables. Many hotel rooms have one, and you open it with a code.

sentence.da: Vi gemmer vigtige papirer og smykker i et **pengeskab**.
sentence.en: We keep important papers and jewelry in a safe.

et pensum.explanation: "Et pensum" means "a syllabus", all the material students must learn for a course. Something that will not be tested is ikke på pensum (not on the syllabus).

sentence.da: Hele bogen er **pensum**, så vi skal læse den.
sentence.en: The whole book is on the syllabus, so we have to read it.

et personalemøde.explanation: "Et personalemøde" means "a staff meeting", a meeting where everyone who works at a place gathers to share news and decide practical things. The first part, personale, means the staff.

sentence.da: Alle lærerne mødes til et **personalemøde** hver mandag.
sentence.en: All the teachers meet at a staff meeting every Monday.

et perspektiv.explanation: "Et perspektiv" means "a perspective", a particular way of seeing something: Det er et interessant perspektiv (That is an interesting perspective). In drawing, it is also the way lines make a flat picture look deep.

sentence.da: Børn og voksne har ikke det samme **perspektiv** på verden.
sentence.en: Children and adults do not have the same perspective on the world.

et pindsvin.explanation: "Et pindsvin" means "a hedgehog", a small, round animal that sleeps through the winter and often lives in gardens. It is built from pind (stick) and svin (hog), so it is literally a stick hog.

sentence.da: Et **pindsvin** har pigge på ryggen og kan rulle sig sammen.
sentence.en: A hedgehog has spines on its back and can roll up into a ball.

et piskeris.explanation: "Et piskeris" means "a whisk", a kitchen tool of wire loops. It is built from at piske (to whip) and ris (twigs).

sentence.da: Jeg rører æg og mel med et **piskeris**.
sentence.en: I mix eggs and flour with a whisk.

et plaster.explanation: "Et plaster" means "a band-aid", a small sticky bandage for a cut.

sentence.da: Sæt et **plaster** på såret.
sentence.en: Put a band-aid on the wound.

et plejebarn.explanation: "Et plejebarn" means "a foster child", a child who lives with another family because the child's own parents cannot look after it. Unlike et adoptivbarn (an adopted child), a foster child does not become the legal child of the new family.

sentence.da: Et **plejebarn** bor hos en anden familie, fordi forældrene ikke kan passe det.
sentence.en: A foster child lives with another family because the parents cannot take care of it.

et point.explanation: "Et point" means "a point" in a game or test: Vi vandt med to point (We won by two points). A point in a discussion is en pointe: Det var en god pointe (That was a good point).

sentence.da: Vi mangler kun et **point** for at vinde.
sentence.en: We only need one more point to win.

et postbud.explanation: "Et postbud" means "a mail carrier", the person who brings letters to your home. You will also hear en postmand (a mailman).

sentence.da: Et **postbud** står ved døren med en pakke.
sentence.en: A mail carrier is at the door with a package.

et posthus.explanation: "Et posthus" means "a post office", the place you go to send and pick up mail. It is built from post (mail) and hus (house).

sentence.da: Jeg skal sende en pakke fra et **posthus**.
sentence.en: I have to send a package from a post office.

et postkontor.explanation: "Et postkontor" means "a post office", where you send letters and packages. It is built from post (mail) and kontor (office). You may also hear et posthus (a post office), which means the same.

sentence.da: Jeg sender en pakke på et **postkontor**.
sentence.en: I send a package at a post office.

et postkort.explanation: "Et postkort" means "a postcard", a card you send by mail. It is built from post (mail) and kort (card).

sentence.da: På ferie sender jeg et **postkort** hjem.
sentence.en: On vacation, I send a postcard home.

et postnummer.explanation: "Et postnummer" means "a postal code", the four digits of a Danish address: 2100 København Ø (2100 Copenhagen Ø). It comes before the town and after the street and house number.

sentence.da: Hvad er dit **postnummer**, så jeg kan sende pakken?
sentence.en: What is your postal code, so I can send the package?

et potentiale.explanation: "Et potentiale" means "a potential", what someone or something could become with time and effort. It is often used without et: Der er potentiale i idéen (There is potential in the idea).

sentence.da: Den unge spiller har et stort **potentiale**, men skal træne mere.
sentence.en: The young player has great potential but needs to train more.

et princip.explanation: "Et princip" means "a principle", a basic belief that guides what you do. Two set phrases are worth knowing: af princip (on principle), as in Jeg spiser ikke kød af princip (I do not eat meat on principle), and i princip (in principle), as in I princip kan alle komme (In principle, anyone can come).

sentence.da: Det er et vigtigt **princip**, at alle får samme chance.
sentence.en: It is an important principle that everyone gets the same chance.

et prisfald.explanation: "Et prisfald" means "a price drop", when something becomes cheaper. It is built from pris (price) and fald (fall).

sentence.da: Efter jul kommer der ofte et **prisfald**.
sentence.en: After Christmas there is often a price drop.

et prisskilt.explanation: "Et prisskilt" means "a price tag", the small sign or label that shows what something costs. It is built from pris (price) and skilt (sign).

sentence.da: Prisen står på et **prisskilt** ved jakken.
sentence.en: The price is on a price tag by the jacket.

et problem.explanation: "Et problem" means "a problem". Det er ikke noget problem means "It is no problem". Hvad er problemet? means "What is the problem?".

sentence.da: Vi har et **problem** med bilen.
sentence.en: We have a problem with the car.

et produkt.explanation: "Et produkt" means "a product", something made to be sold. Items on shop shelves are also called varer (goods).

sentence.da: Vi sælger et nyt **produkt** i butikken.
sentence.en: We sell a new product in the shop.

et program.explanation: "Et program" means "a program", on a computer. It also means a plan or schedule: Hvad er programmet i dag? (What is the plan today?).

sentence.da: Jeg skal installere et nyt **program** på min computer.
sentence.en: I have to install a new program on my computer.

et projekt.explanation: "Et projekt" means "a project", work with a goal and an end: Mit projekt er at male huset (My project is to paint the house).

sentence.da: Vi arbejder på et stort **projekt** sammen.
sentence.en: We are working on a big project together.

et prøverum.explanation: "Et prøverum" means "a fitting room", the little booth in a store, with a curtain or a door, where you check how something fits. It is built from at prøve (to try) and et rum (a room).

sentence.da: Jeg prøver bukserne i et **prøverum**.
sentence.en: I try on the pants in a fitting room.

et pseudonym.explanation: "Et pseudonym" means "a pseudonym", a made-up name that someone uses instead of their real name, often a writer or an artist who wants to stay unknown.

sentence.da: Forfatteren skrev bøgerne under et **pseudonym**, så ingen kendte hendes rigtige navn.
sentence.en: The author wrote the books under a pseudonym, so no one knew her real name.

et pudebetræk.explanation: "Et pudebetræk" means "a pillowcase". It is built from pude (pillow) and betræk (cover), and betræk also appears in et sofabetræk (a sofa cover).

sentence.da: Jeg putter puden i et **pudebetræk**.
sentence.en: I put the pillow in a pillowcase.

et pulver.explanation: "Et pulver" means "a powder", something dry and fine. You find it in bagepulver (baking powder).

sentence.da: Rør **pulver** ud i varmt vand.
sentence.en: Stir powder into hot water.

et pund.explanation: "Et pund" means "a pound", both the British money and the weight. In Danish, the weight is about 500 grams, a little more than a US pound.

sentence.da: Billetten til London koster tyve **pund**.
sentence.en: The ticket to London costs twenty pounds.

et punkt.explanation: "Et punkt" means "a point", a spot or an item on a list: Hotellet ligger på det røde punkt på kortet (The hotel is at the red spot on the map). A period at the end of a sentence is et punktum.

sentence.da: Det første **punkt** på listen er mælk.
sentence.en: The first item on the list is milk.

et punktum.explanation: "Et punktum" means "a period", the dot at the end of a sentence. Added to a statement, Punktum! means "That's final!": Jeg har sagt nej, punktum! (I said no, period!)

sentence.da: Der skal være et **punktum** i slutningen af sætningen.
sentence.en: There has to be a period at the end of the sentence.

et puslespil.explanation: "Et puslespil" means "a puzzle", a game where you fit small pieces together into a picture. A riddle to solve is en gåde.

sentence.da: Et **puslespil** har mange små brikker.
sentence.en: A puzzle has many small pieces.

et påfund.explanation: "Et påfund" means "an idea" and "an invention", something that someone has thought up. It often sounds surprised or critical, as in Hvad er det for et påfund? (What kind of idea is that?).

sentence.da: Det er hans eget **påfund**, og ingen andre har prøvet det.
sentence.en: It is his own idea, and nobody else has tried it.

et påskeæg.explanation: "Et påskeæg" means "an Easter egg", often a chocolate egg or a painted egg. It is built from påske (Easter) and æg (egg).

sentence.da: Til påske får jeg et **påskeæg** af chokolade.
sentence.en: At Easter I get an Easter egg made of chocolate.

pandehår.explanation: "Et pandehår" means "bangs", the short hair cut straight across the forehead. Danish uses it in the singular, as one thing, where English says bangs in the plural.

sentence.da: Hendes **pandehår** hænger ned over panden og øjnene.
sentence.en: Her bangs hang down over her forehead and eyes.

panik.explanation: "Panik" means "panic", a sudden, overwhelming feeling that makes people stop thinking clearly. Unlike English, Danish leaves out "a" here: Jeg var i panik (I was in a panic).

sentence.da: Der opstod **panik**, da alarmen gik i gang.
sentence.en: Panic broke out when the alarm went off.

pant.explanation: "Pant" means "deposit": a small extra amount added to the price of a bottle or can, which you get back when you return the empty bottle.

forms.en: to return bottles for the deposit

sentence.da: Der er **pant** på flasken.
sentence.en: There is a deposit on the bottle.

pap.explanation: "Pap" means "cardboard", the thick, stiff material boxes are made of. Do not mix it up with papir (paper): pap is much thicker.

sentence.da: Kassen er lavet af tyk **pap** og er let.
sentence.en: The box is made of thick cardboard and is light.

papir.explanation: "Papir" means "paper", the material you write or print on. In the plural, papirer can also mean documents: Har du dine papirer med? (Do you have your papers with you?)

sentence.da: Jeg printer brevet på **papir**.
sentence.en: I print the letter on paper.

paradoksal.explanation: "Paradoksal" means "paradoxical", seeming to contradict itself even though it may still be true. It is used for situations, results and statements.

sentence.da: Situationen er **paradoksal**: Jo mere han sparer, jo mere bruger han.
sentence.en: The situation is paradoxical: the more he saves, the more he spends.

paranoid.explanation: "Paranoid" means "paranoid", believing without reason that others are against you or watching you. Danes also use it loosely for being too wary of others: Du er helt paranoid (You are totally paranoid).

sentence.da: Han er **paranoid** og tror, at naboerne altid holder øje med ham.
sentence.en: He is paranoid and thinks the neighbors are always watching him.

parat.explanation: "Parat" means "ready", often followed by til (to). In everyday talk, klar is the same idea: Er du klar? (Are you ready?).

sentence.da: Er du **parat** til at gå nu?
sentence.en: Are you ready to go now?

parkeret.explanation: "Parkeret" means "parked", for a vehicle that is standing still. It comes from at parkere (to park).

sentence.da: Bilen er **parkeret** foran huset.
sentence.en: The car is parked in front of the house.

parkering.explanation: "Parkering" means "parking", the place where you may leave a car. The action is at parkere (to park).

sentence.da: Der er gratis **parkering** bag ved hotellet.
sentence.en: There is free parking behind the hotel.

parmesan.explanation: "Parmesan" means "parmesan", a hard, salty Italian cheese that is often grated over pasta.

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have lidt **parmesan** på min pasta.
sentence.en: I would like a little parmesan on my pasta.

pas på.explanation: "Pas på" means "watch out" or "be careful": Pas på, det er varmt (Careful, it is hot). It also means "look after": Pas på børnene (Look after the children).

sentence.da: **Pas på** bilerne!
sentence.en: Watch out for the cars!

pas på dig selv.explanation: "Pas på dig selv" means "take care of yourself" and is a warm way to say goodbye. To several people, say pas på jer selv (take care of yourselves).

forms.da: Pas på dig selv i trafikken.

sentence.da: Farvel! **Pas på dig selv**!
sentence.en: Goodbye! Take care of yourself!

passende.explanation: "Passende" means "suitable" or "appropriate". It can also mean "reasonable": en passende pris (a reasonable price).

sentence.da: Jeg leder efter noget **passende** at tage på til festen.
sentence.en: I am looking for something suitable to wear to the party.

passiv.explanation: "Passiv" means "passive", not taking action or joining in. In grammar, a passive sentence tells what happened to something: Bilen blev stjålet (The car was stolen).

sentence.da: Hun var **passiv** i timen og sagde aldrig noget.
sentence.en: She was passive in class and never said anything.

pasta.explanation: "Pasta" means "pasta", the Italian food made from wheat dough. You do not count it, so you say Jeg laver pasta (I am making pasta) with nothing in front of it.

sentence.da: Spaghetti er en slags **pasta**.
sentence.en: Spaghetti is a kind of pasta.
