peber.explanation: "Peber" means "pepper", the spice you put on food. It is normally used without en or et: Jeg bruger peber på kødet (I use pepper on the meat). Do not mix it up with peberfrugt (bell pepper), which is a vegetable.

sentence.da: Jeg tilføjer lidt salt og **peber**.
sentence.en: I add a little salt and pepper.

penge.explanation: "Penge" means "money". It is always "many", never one, so you never say en or et before it. For one coin or one note, say en mønt (a coin) or en seddel (a banknote).

sentence.da: Man betaler med **penge**.
sentence.en: You pay with money.

pensioneret.explanation: "Pensioneret" means "retired", no longer working because of age.

sentence.da: Min far er **pensioneret** og har meget tid.
sentence.en: My father is retired and has a lot of time.

perfekt.explanation: "Perfekt" means "perfect". On its own it works as an exclamation: Perfekt! means "Great, that works!".

sentence.da: Et **perfekt** svar har ingen fejl.
sentence.en: A perfect answer has no mistakes.

permanent.explanation: "Permanent" means "permanent", meant to stay for good, not just for a while. The opposite is midlertidig (temporary).

sentence.da: Han har et **permanent** job i en bank.
sentence.en: He has a permanent job at a bank.

persille.explanation: "Persille" means "parsley", a green herb often sprinkled on food at the end.

sentence.da: Jeg drysser frisk **persille** på kartoflerne.
sentence.en: I sprinkle fresh parsley on the potatoes.

personale.explanation: "Et personale" means "staff", all the people who work at a shop, hospital or company. It names the group as a whole. For one person, say en medarbejder (an employee).

sentence.da: Sygeplejersker og læger er en del af hospitalets **personale**.
sentence.en: Nurses and doctors are part of the hospital's staff.

personlig.explanation: "Personlig" means "personal", for what is about you as a person: Det er et personligt spørgsmål (That is a personal question). It also fits things with your own style: en personlig stil (a personal style).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **personlig** mening om det.
sentence.en: I have a personal opinion about it.

personligt.explanation: "Personligt" means "personally" and starts a sentence with your own opinion: Personligt kan jeg godt lide vinteren (Personally, I like winter). It also means "in person": Jeg har mødt hende personligt (I have met her in person).

sentence.da: **Personligt** kan jeg godt lide den nye film.
sentence.en: Personally, I like the new movie.

pervers.explanation: "Pervers" means "perverted", a strong, negative word for behavior seen as sick or morally wrong, often sexual. It can also mean "perverse", against what is reasonable: det er pervers, at ... (it is perverse that ...).

sentence.da: Hans humor er **pervers**, og folk bliver ofte stødt.
sentence.en: His humor is perverted, and people are often offended.

pessimistisk.explanation: "Pessimistisk" means "pessimistic", expecting things to go badly. It describes a person's mood or a way of looking at things, such as a forecast.

sentence.da: Han er **pessimistisk** og tror altid, at det går galt.
sentence.en: He is pessimistic and always thinks it will go wrong.

pinlig.explanation: "Pinlig" means "embarrassing" and describes the situation. To say how you feel, use flov: Jeg er flov (I am embarrassed).

sentence.da: Den situation var meget **pinlig**.
sentence.en: That situation was very embarrassing.

pinse.explanation: "En pinse" means "Pentecost" or "Whitsun", a church holiday seven weeks after Easter. In Denmark Pinsedag (Whit Sunday) and Anden pinsedag (Whit Monday) are days off, so it is a long weekend.

sentence.da: Til **pinse** er der en ekstra fridag om mandagen.
sentence.en: At Pentecost there is an extra day off on Monday.

piskefløde.explanation: "Piskefløde" means "whipping cream", cream with enough fat that you can whip it. It is built from at piske (to whip) and fløde (cream). Cream for coffee is called kaffefløde.

forms.en: The cake has whipping cream in it.

sentence.da: Vi pisker **piskefløde** til kagen.
sentence.en: We whip whipping cream for the cake.

pjat.explanation: "Pjat" means "nonsense". Use it to wave off an idea: Han taler pjat (He is talking nonsense). Said alone, Pjat! is a quick, light way to say you don't believe it.

sentence.da: Det er noget **pjat**, og jeg tror ikke på det.
sentence.en: That is nonsense, and I don't believe it.

placeret.explanation: "Placeret" means "placed" or "located", saying where something is. With højt (high) it also means high-ranking: en højt placeret politiker (a high-ranking politician).

sentence.da: Skolen er **placeret** midt i byen, tæt på stationen.
sentence.en: The school is located in the middle of town, close to the station.

pladsmangel.explanation: "En pladsmangel" means "lack of space", not enough room for people or things. Danish often builds words like this with mangel on the end, for example vandmangel (lack of water).

forms.en: lack of space in the apartment

sentence.da: Der er **pladsmangel** i garagen, og der kan ikke stå flere biler.
sentence.en: There is a lack of space in the garage, and no more cars can fit.

planlægning.explanation: "Planlægning" means "planning": Der er brug for mere planlægning (More planning is needed). You say planlægning af (planning of) to name what is planned.

sentence.da: Før festen er der meget **planlægning**.
sentence.en: Before the party there is a lot of planning.

plastik.explanation: "Plastik" means "plastic". Many words start with it, like plastikaffald (plastic waste).

sentence.da: Flasken er lavet af **plastik**, ikke glas.
sentence.en: The bottle is made of plastic, not glass.

plastikaffald.explanation: "Plastikaffald" means "plastic waste", trash made of plastic such as bottles and bags. Danish builds many words from a material plus affald, such as madaffald (food waste).

sentence.da: Tomme flasker og poser af plastik er **plastikaffald**.
sentence.en: Empty bottles and bags made of plastic are plastic waste.

plat.explanation: "Plat" means "vulgar" or "cheesy", used for jokes, remarks and entertainment that feel crude or cheap. It criticizes taste.

sentence.da: Hans humor er **plat**, og kun få griner af den.
sentence.en: His humor is cheesy, and few people laugh at it.

pleje.explanation: "En pleje" means "care", looking after someone who is sick or old, or after your body. It is practical care, unlike omsorg (warm concern). The verb at pleje also means "to usually do": Jeg plejer at stå tidligt op (I usually get up early).

sentence.da: På sygehuset arbejder hun med **pleje** af syge.
sentence.en: At the hospital she works caring for sick people.

pludselig.explanation: "Pludselig" means "suddenly" and also "sudden". Pludselig kom han ind (Suddenly he came in). Lige pludselig is a bit stronger, like "all of a sudden".

sentence.da: **Pludselig** hørte jeg et højt brag.
sentence.en: Suddenly I heard a loud bang.

poesi.explanation: "En poesi" means "poetry", written art that plays with sound and images. It also means a beautiful, dreamlike quality in something: Der er poesi i den gamle by (There is poetry in the old town).

sentence.da: I **poesi** står ordene ofte i korte linjer og med rim.
sentence.en: In poetry the words are often in short lines and with rhyme.

polen.explanation: "Polen" means "Poland". Use i (in) for being there and til (to) for going there: Jeg bor i Polen (I live in Poland); Vi rejser til Polen (We are traveling to Poland).

sentence.da: Warszawa ligger i **Polen**.
sentence.en: Warsaw is in Poland.

politi.explanation: "Politi" means "police" and is used without en (a). Danish treats it as one thing, so you say politiet er her (the police are here). One officer is en politibetjent (a police officer).

sentence.da: **Politi** og ambulance er kommet.
sentence.en: The police and an ambulance have arrived.

politisk.explanation: "Politisk" means "political" and fits things about how a country is run. Politics itself is politik.

sentence.da: Det er en **politisk** beslutning, ikke min.
sentence.en: It is a political decision, not mine.

polsk.explanation: "Polsk" means "Polish", for things from Poland and for the language: Jeg taler polsk (I speak Polish).

sentence.da: Min nabo kommer fra Polen og taler **polsk**.
sentence.en: My neighbor comes from Poland and speaks Polish.

polyester.explanation: "En polyester" means "polyester", a man-made fabric used for clothes and sports gear. It dries quickly and does not wrinkle easily.

sentence.da: Mærket i trøjen viser, at den er lavet af **polyester**.
sentence.en: The label in the sweater shows that it is made of polyester.

pommes frites.explanation: "Pommes frites" means "French fries". Danes often shorten it to pommes (fries).

sentence.da: **Pommes frites** er lavet af kartofler.
sentence.en: French fries are made of potatoes.

popcorn.explanation: "Popcorn" means "popcorn" and is spelled as in English. You count it by the container: en spand popcorn (a bucket of popcorn).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **popcorn**, før filmen starter.
sentence.en: I buy popcorn before the movie starts.

populær.explanation: "Populær" means "popular", for people, places and things that many people enjoy.

sentence.da: Det er en **populær** café, så vi bestiller bord.
sentence.en: It is a popular café, so we are booking a table.

porcelæn.explanation: "Porcelæn" means "china" or "porcelain", a fine, hard ceramic used for plates, cups and vases. Danes also use it for the dishes themselves: det fine porcelæn (the good china).

sentence.da: Tallerkener og kopper af **porcelæn** går let i stykker.
sentence.en: Plates and cups made of porcelain break easily.

porto.explanation: "Porto" means "postage", the price for sending a letter or package. You pay it for the sending, not for what is inside.

sentence.da: Hvor meget er **porto** til et brev til Tyskland?
sentence.en: How much is postage for a letter to Germany?

positiv.explanation: "Positiv" means "positive", for good news and feelings, and for a person who looks on the bright side. The opposite is negativ (negative).

sentence.da: Han har en meget **positiv** holdning.
sentence.en: He has a very positive attitude.

positivt.explanation: "Positivt" means "positively", in a good or hopeful way. It often follows verbs like tænke (think), svare (answer) and reagere (react).

sentence.da: Chefen reagerede **positivt** på forslaget og sagde ja.
sentence.en: The boss reacted positively to the proposal and said yes.

post.explanation: "Post" means "mail": the letters and parcels that arrive. It is also the word for the postal service that brings them.

sentence.da: Postbuddet kommer hver dag med **post** til os.
sentence.en: The mail carrier comes every day with mail for us.

pragtfuld.explanation: "Pragtfuld" means "splendid": magnificent and beautiful, often about views, buildings, nature or colors. It is built from pragt (splendor) and -fuld (full of), so it is something full of splendor.

sentence.da: Fra tårnet er udsigten over byen og havet **pragtfuld**.
sentence.en: From the tower, the view over the city and the sea is splendid.

praktisk.explanation: "Praktisk" means "practical" and "handy", for things that are useful in daily life. About a person, it means good with your hands: Jeg er ikke så praktisk (I am not very handy).

sentence.da: Den lille taske er meget **praktisk** på ture.
sentence.en: The small bag is very practical on trips.

pressefrihed.explanation: "Pressefrihed" means "freedom of the press", the right of the media and reporters to publish what they find without government control.

forms.en: freedom of the press in Denmark

sentence.da: Med **pressefrihed** må journalister skrive om politikerne uden at blive straffet.
sentence.en: With freedom of the press, journalists may write about the politicians without being punished.

prikket.explanation: "Prikket" means "polka-dotted", covered in small round dots, mostly for fabric and patterns. It comes from en prik (a dot).

sentence.da: Hendes kjole er rød og **prikket**, ligesom en mariehøne.
sentence.en: Her dress is red and polka-dotted, like a ladybug.

primær.explanation: "Primær" means "primary", the first or main one of several. It is used for goals, reasons, users and sources.

sentence.da: Årsagen er **primær**, og de andre er mindre vigtige.
sentence.en: The reason is primary, and the others are less important.

primært.explanation: "Primært" means "primarily", mostly or above all, saying what the main part of something is. The word primær (primary) describes a thing instead: det primære mål (the primary goal).

sentence.da: Butikken sælger **primært** brugt tøj, men også lidt legetøj.
sentence.en: The store sells mostly used clothes, but also a few toys.

privat.explanation: "Privat" means "private", for what belongs to one person or family and not to everyone.

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke tale om noget **privat**.
sentence.en: I do not want to talk about anything private.

privatliv.explanation: "Et privatliv" means "privacy" and "private life", the part of your life that belongs to you and not to work or the public.

sentence.da: Politikere har også ret til et **privatliv** uden kameraer.
sentence.en: Politicians also have a right to a private life without cameras.

problematisk.explanation: "Problematisk" means "problematic", for a situation, plan or habit that brings problems. It is built on et problem (a problem): en problematisk situation is one that causes trouble.

sentence.da: Det er **problematisk**, når ingen har ansvaret.
sentence.en: It is problematic when nobody is responsible.

problemfri.explanation: "Problemfri" means "problem-free", going well, with no trouble. The ending -fri (free) means "without" in many words: sukkerfri (sugar-free), glutenfri (gluten-free).

sentence.da: Flyveturen var **problemfri**, og vi landede til tiden.
sentence.en: The flight was trouble-free, and we landed on time.

produktiv.explanation: "Produktiv" means "productive", getting a lot done or producing a lot. It describes a person or a method that gets results, not just one that is busy: Jeg var travl, men ikke produktiv (I was busy, but not productive).

sentence.da: Hun er meget **produktiv** og skriver tre sider om dagen.
sentence.en: She is very productive and writes three pages a day.

professionel.explanation: "Professionel" means "professional", done as a paid job or at a high level. It also means skilled and well done: professionelt arbejde (professional work).

sentence.da: Hun er **professionel** fodboldspiller og træner hver dag.
sentence.en: She is a professional soccer player and trains every day.

protein.explanation: "Et protein" means "a protein", the nutrient the body uses to build and repair muscles. Without et, it names the nutrient as a whole: Æg indeholder meget protein (Eggs contain a lot of protein).

sentence.da: Kød, fisk og bønner er gode kilder til **protein**.
sentence.en: Meat, fish and beans are good sources of protein.

præcis.explanation: "Præcis" means "exactly". Compare Det koster præcis hundrede kroner (It costs exactly a hundred kroner) with Det koster cirka hundrede kroner (It costs about a hundred kroner). On its own, Præcis! means "Exactly!" or "That's right!".

sentence.da: Toget kommer **præcis** klokken otte.
sentence.en: The train arrives at exactly eight o'clock.

psykiatrisk.explanation: "Psykiatrisk" means "psychiatric", about the medical care of serious mental illness. It is the medical word; for the mind and feelings in general, Danes say psykisk (mental).

sentence.da: Hun blev indlagt på en **psykiatrisk** afdeling på hospitalet.
sentence.en: She was admitted to a psychiatric ward at the hospital.

psykisk.explanation: "Psykisk" means "mental" or "psychological", about the mind and feelings, not the body. Its opposite is fysisk (physical): fysisk og psykisk sundhed (physical and mental health).

sentence.da: Stress er en **psykisk** belastning, men kroppen mærker den også.
sentence.en: Stress is a mental strain, but the body feels it too.

publikum.explanation: "Et publikum" means "an audience", all the people who watch or listen at a concert, a play or a match. It names the whole group at once and is used in the singular, so a crowd of thousands is still just et publikum.

sentence.da: **Publikum** klappede længe, da sangeren forlod scenen.
sentence.en: The audience clapped for a long time when the singer left the stage.

pudsig.explanation: "Pudsig" means "funny" or "odd" in a sweet way: something that makes you smile rather than laugh out loud. It is often said about small animals, children and little habits. A joke or a party is sjov (fun) instead.

sentence.da: Hvalpen løber på en **pudsig** måde og får os til at smile.
sentence.en: The puppy runs in a funny way and makes us smile.

punktlig.explanation: "Punktlig" means "punctual", the habit of showing up or finishing right when agreed. For one single occasion, use til tiden (on time): Jeg kom til tiden (I arrived on time).

sentence.da: Hun er altid **punktlig** og kommer aldrig for sent til møder.
sentence.en: She is always punctual and never comes late to meetings.

purløg.explanation: "Purløg" means "chives", thin green stalks you cut small and sprinkle on food. It is not an onion, even though et løg (an onion) is in the word.

sentence.da: Jeg klipper **purløg** ud over suppen.
sentence.en: I snip chives over the soup.

pynt.explanation: "Pynt" means "decoration(s)", things that make a place look nice. It stays the same for one or many.

sentence.da: Vi hængte **pynt** op i stuen før festen.
sentence.en: We hung decorations in the living room before the party.

pyt.explanation: "Pyt" means "never mind" and lets a small problem go. Say it after a small mistake: Pyt, jeg tørrer det op (Never mind, I'll wipe it up). It is friendly and relaxed.

forms.da: Pyt, det er ikke så vigtigt.
forms.en: Never mind, it is not that important.

sentence.da: **Pyt**, vi tager bare den næste bus.
sentence.en: Never mind, we'll just take the next bus.

på.explanation: "På" means "on", but also "at" or "in": på arbejde (at work), på ferie (on vacation), på dansk (in Danish). It is also used with islands and streets: på Fyn (on Funen), på gaden (on the street).

sentence.da: Telefonen ligger **på** bordet.
sentence.en: The phone is on the table.

på deltid.explanation: "På deltid" means "part-time", for a shorter week than normal. It is built from del (part) and tid (time). Del also works alone: en del af ugen (a part of the week).

sentence.da: Min søster arbejder **på deltid** i en butik.
sentence.en: My sister works part-time in a store.

på den anden side.explanation: "På den anden side" means "on the other hand" and gives a second view that balances the first. Anden is the word for other here.

forms.da: på den anden side af vejen
forms.en: on the other side of the road

forms.da: På den anden side kan jeg vente.
forms.en: On the other hand, I can wait.

related.en: in return, on the other hand

sentence.da: Bilen er gammel, men **på den anden side** er den billig.
sentence.en: The car is old, but on the other hand it is cheap.

på den ene side.explanation: "På den ene side" means "on one hand" and starts the first of two views. The second view usually follows after men (but).

forms.da: på den ene side af huset
forms.en: on one side of the house

forms.da: På den ene side er det nemt.
forms.en: On one hand it is easy.

related.en: on the other hand, by contrast
on the other hand, in return

sentence.da: **På den ene side** vil jeg rejse, men jeg er også bange.
sentence.en: On one hand I want to travel, but I am also afraid.

på forhånd.explanation: "På forhånd" means "in advance", before something happens. At the end of a request it means "thank you for doing it": Kan du sende filen? Tak på forhånd! (Can you send the file? Thanks in advance!)

sentence.da: Du skal booke bordet **på forhånd**.
sentence.en: You must book the table in advance.

på fuldtid.explanation: "På fuldtid" means "full-time", for the usual number of hours in a job. It is built from fuld (full) and tid (time). Fuld on its own can also mean drunk: Han er fuld (He is drunk).

sentence.da: Hun arbejder **på fuldtid** og kommer hjem sent.
sentence.en: She works full-time and comes home late.

på gensyn.explanation: "På gensyn" means "until we see each other again" and is a polite, slightly formal goodbye. With friends, vi ses (see you) is more usual.

sentence.da: Tak for besøget. **På gensyn!**
sentence.en: Thanks for the visit. See you again!

på grund af.explanation: "På grund af" means "because of" and goes before a thing. To give a reason with a full sentence, use fordi (because): på grund af regnen (because of the rain), but fordi det regner (because it is raining).

sentence.da: Vi kom for sent **på grund af** trafikken.
sentence.en: We were late because of the traffic.

på tide.explanation: "På tide" means "about time" and says that something should happen now. Said on its own, Det er på tide! means "It's about time!", often when something has waited too long.

forms.da: Det er på tide at stå op.
forms.en: It is time to get up.

forms.da: Det er på tide med en pause.
forms.en: It is time for a break.

sentence.da: Det er **på tide** at gå i seng.
sentence.en: It is time to go to bed.

på tilbud.explanation: "På tilbud" means "on sale", for something sold at a lower price than usual. Tilbud on its own means "offer", so på tilbud is literally "on offer".

sentence.da: Kaffen er **på tilbud** i dag.
sentence.en: The coffee is on sale today.

på trods af.explanation: "På trods af" means "despite" and goes before a thing. It says that something happened in spite of something in the way.

sentence.da: Vi tog af sted **på trods af** regnen.
sentence.en: We set off despite the rain.

på vej.explanation: "På vej" means "on the way", and it works for people and for things. Add where you are going with hjem (home) or til (to): på vej til arbejde (on the way to work).

forms.en: The bus is on its way.

sentence.da: Jeg er **på vej** hjem nu.
sentence.en: I am on my way home now.

påfaldende.explanation: "Påfaldende" means "striking": so unusual that you cannot help noticing it. It often points to something odd, not just something beautiful. It can also strengthen another describing word: Han var påfaldende stille (He was oddly quiet).

sentence.da: Hans tavshed var **påfaldende**, når alle andre talte.
sentence.en: His silence was striking when everyone else was talking.

pålidelig.explanation: "Pålidelig" means "reliable", someone or something you can count on to do what is expected. It is about dependable performance; troværdig (believable) is more about whether you believe what is said.

sentence.da: Han er en **pålidelig** kollega, som altid gør, hvad han lover.
sentence.en: He is a reliable colleague who always does what he promises.

pålæg.explanation: "Pålæg" means "cold cuts" or "sandwich toppings", anything you lay on a slice, such as ham, cheese or liver pâté.

sentence.da: Hvilket **pålæg** vil du have på dit rugbrød?
sentence.en: Which topping do you want on your rye bread?

påske.explanation: "Påske" means "Easter". Use it with no a or the in til påske (at Easter). To say during Easter, use i påsken. The greeting is Glædelig påske! (Happy Easter!).

sentence.da: Til **påske** maler børnene æg.
sentence.en: At Easter the children paint eggs.

påskedag.explanation: "Påskedag" means "Easter Sunday", the main day of Easter. The day after is called anden påskedag (Easter Monday), and both are public holidays in Denmark.

sentence.da: **Påskedag** falder altid på en søndag i marts eller april.
sentence.en: Easter Sunday always falls on a Sunday in March or April.

påtrængende.explanation: "Påtrængende" means "pushy" or "pressing": something that forces itself on you and is hard to ignore. About a person, it means too eager and not leaving you alone. About a need, it means urgent: et påtrængende behov (a pressing need).

sentence.da: Sælgeren var **påtrængende** og fulgte efter mig rundt i butikken.
sentence.en: The salesman was pushy and followed me around the store.

pæn.explanation: "Pæn" means "nice-looking" or "neat": Værelset er pænt (The room is neat). It also means "well-behaved": Vær pæn (Be good).

sentence.da: Du ser **pæn** ud i den nye kjole.
sentence.en: You look nice in the new dress.
